Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ১) What is ganglia?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.option1: small aggregates of nerve cells inside the CNS
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.option2: small aggregates of nerve cells outside the CNS
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.option3: small aggregates of neuroglia inside the CNS
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.option4: small aggregates of neuroglia outside the CNS
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
A ganglion is a collection or aggregate of neuronal cell bodies located outside the central nervous system (CNS), i.e., in the peripheral nervous system (PNS).

  • Ganglion → neuronal cell bodies outside CNS

  • Nucleus → neuronal cell bodies inside CNS

  • Neuroglial cells → support neurons, not the main component of ganglia

High-yield Neuroanatomy recall:
CNS → Nucleus
PNS → Ganglion

Exam pearl:
“Ganglion = collection of nerve cell bodies in the PNS.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ২) Which is not one of the specific layers of skin?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
The skin proper consists of two main layers:

  1. Epidermis

  2. Dermis, which is further divided into:

    • Papillary layer

    • Reticular layer

The subcutaneous layer (hypodermis) lies beneath the skin and is not considered a specific layer of the skin proper.

High-yield Skin anatomy recall:
Skin = Epidermis + Dermis
Dermis = Papillary + Reticular
Subcutaneous tissue = below the skin

Exam pearl:
“Subcutaneous layer is beneath the skin, not part of skin proper.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ৩) Visible part of the ear is called.....?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
The pinna (auricle) is the visible external part of the ear. It is mainly composed of elastic cartilage and functions to collect and direct sound waves into the external auditory canal.

  • Pinna/Auricle → visible external ear

  • Eardrum (tympanic membrane) → separates external and middle ear

  • Stapes → middle-ear ossicle

  • Cuticle → not an ear structure

High-yield Ear anatomy recall:
External ear → Pinna + external auditory canal + tympanic membrane

Exam pearl:
“Visible part of ear = Pinna (auricle).”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ৪) Which dermatome has maximum area of distribution in lower limb?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
Among the given options, S2 dermatome has the largest area of cutaneous distribution in the lower limb. It supplies much of the posterior aspect of the thigh and leg.

  • S1 → lateral foot and little toe

  • S2 → posterior thigh and much of posterior leg

  • S3 → buttock/perineal region

  • S4 → perianal region

High-yield Dermatome recall:
S1 → lateral foot
S2 → posterior thigh
S3–S5 → buttock/perineal (“saddle”) region

Exam pearl:
“Among S1–S4, S2 has the largest lower-limb dermatome.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ৫) The nervous system develops from which germ layer?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
The nervous system develops primarily from the ectoderm, specifically from the neural plate, which folds to form the neural tube. The neural tube gives rise to the brain and spinal cord, while the neural crest contributes to much of the peripheral nervous system.

  • Ectoderm → nervous system + epidermis

  • Mesoderm → muscles, bones, connective tissue, cardiovascular system

  • Endoderm → gastrointestinal and respiratory epithelium

High-yield Embryology recall:
Neural plate → neural tube → CNS
Neural crest → much of PNS

Exam pearl:
“Nervous system = ectoderm.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ৬) The part of a hair extending beyond the skin surface is called.....?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
The hair shaft is the portion of the hair that extends above the surface of the skin and is visible externally. It consists mainly of dead, keratinized cells.

  • Hair shaft → above the skin surface

  • Hair root → below the skin surface

  • Hair bulb → enlarged base of the hair root

  • Dermal papilla → connective tissue structure within the hair bulb that supplies nutrients

High-yield Skin histology recall:
Hair shaft = above skin
Hair root + bulb = below skin

Exam pearl:
“Visible portion of hair = hair shaft.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ৭) The Tympanic membrane is connected to.....?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
The tympanic membrane is directly attached to the handle (manubrium) of the malleus, the first ossicle of the middle ear. Vibrations of the tympanic membrane are therefore transmitted to the malleus → incus → stapes.

  • Tympanic membrane → Malleus

  • Malleus → Incus → Stapes

  • Tensor tympani → attaches to malleus and helps tense the tympanic membrane

High-yield Ear anatomy recall:
Tympanic membrane → malleus → incus → stapes → oval window.

Exam pearl:
“Tympanic membrane is attached to the handle of malleus.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ৮) Most neurons have how many main parts?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
Most neurons have three main parts:

  1. Cell body (soma/perikaryon) — contains the nucleus and metabolic machinery.

  2. Dendrites — receive signals from other neurons or receptors.

  3. Axon — carries nerve impulses away from the cell body.

High-yield Neuroanatomy recall:
Neuron = Cell body + Dendrites + Axon

Exam pearl:
“Three main parts of a neuron: soma, dendrites, and axon.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ৯) The distal end of the plate becomes free of the nail bed at the epidermal fold called the........?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
The hyponychium is the epidermal region beneath the free distal edge of the nail, where the nail plate separates from the nail bed.

  • Hyponychium → beneath the free edge of the nail

  • Eponychium → proximal nail fold

  • Cuticle → thin keratinized extension of eponychium over the nail plate

  • Nail matrix → produces the nail plate

High-yield Nail anatomy recall:
Proximal nail fold → eponychium/cuticle
Free distal nail edge → hyponychium

Exam pearl:
“Hyponychium = under the free edge of the nail.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ১০) Which layer is seen only in thick skin?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
Stratum lucidum is a thin, translucent layer of the epidermis found only in thick skin, especially on the palms and soles.

The layers of epidermis from deep to superficial are:

Stratum basale → Stratum spinosum → Stratum granulosum → Stratum lucidum → Stratum corneum

High-yield Skin histology recall:
Thick skin → has stratum lucidum + no hair follicles/sebaceous glands.

Exam pearl:
“Lucidum = thick skin (palms & soles).”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ১১) Outer bony Labyrinth is filled with a fluid called.......?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
The bony labyrinth of the inner ear is filled with perilymph, while the membranous labyrinth is filled with endolymph.

  • Bony labyrinth → Perilymph

  • Membranous labyrinth → Endolymph

High-yield Ear anatomy recall:
Perilymph → outside the membranous labyrinth
Endolymph → inside the membranous labyrinth

Exam pearl:
“Bony = Perilymph; Membranous = Endolymph.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ১২) Which type of neurons are the most common?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
Multipolar neurons are the most common type of neuron in the human nervous system. They have one axon and multiple dendrites and are commonly found as motor neurons and interneurons in the CNS.

  • Multipolar → most common

  • Bipolar → retina, olfactory pathway, vestibulocochlear ganglia

  • Pseudounipolar → sensory neurons of dorsal root ganglia

  • Unipolar → rare in adult humans

High-yield Neuroanatomy recall:
Multipolar = most common + one axon + many dendrites.

Exam pearl:
“Most neurons in humans are multipolar.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ১৩) The acini of sebaceous glands are the classic example of............secretion?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
Sebaceous glands are the classic example of holocrine secretion. In holocrine secretion, the entire secretory cell disintegrates and releases its contents as the secretion.

  • Sebaceous gland → Holocrine

  • Apocrine → apical portion of cell is pinched off

  • Eccrine → secretion by exocytosis without loss of cell cytoplasm

  • Norcrine → not a standard mode of glandular secretion

High-yield Histology recall:
Holocrine → whole cell destroyed → sebaceous gland
Apocrine → apical part lost → mammary gland (classically)
Eccrine → cell remains intact → sweat gland

Exam pearl:
“Sebaceous = Holocrine.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ১৪) What is the dermatome of umbilicus?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
The umbilicus corresponds to the T10 dermatome. This is a classic landmark used in clinical neurological examination.

High-yield Dermatome recall:

  • T4 → nipple

  • T6 → xiphisternum

  • T10 → umbilicus

  • L1 → inguinal region

Exam pearl:
“T10 = Umbilicus.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ১৫) Nissl granules are composed of.....?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
Nissl granules (Nissl bodies) are accumulations of rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) and associated ribosomes in the neuronal cell body and dendrites. They are responsible for protein synthesis in neurons.

  • Nissl granules → RER + ribosomes

  • Present → cell body and dendrites

  • Absent → axon and axon hillock

High-yield Neurohistology recall:
Nissl substance = RER + ribosomes → protein synthesis.

Exam pearl:
“Nissl granules = RER.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ১৬) How many semicircular canals are present in the Inner ear?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
The inner ear contains three semicircular canals:

  1. Anterior (superior) semicircular canal

  2. Posterior semicircular canal

  3. Lateral (horizontal) semicircular canal

They are part of the vestibular apparatus and detect angular/rotational acceleration, helping maintain balance.

High-yield Ear anatomy recall:
3 semicircular canals → anterior + posterior + lateral.

Exam pearl:
“Semicircular canals = 3.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ১৭) Schwann cell corresponds to which cell in CNS?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
Schwann cells form the myelin sheath in the peripheral nervous system (PNS). Their functional counterpart in the central nervous system (CNS) is the oligodendrocyte, which produces myelin around CNS axons.

  • PNS → Schwann cell → myelin

  • CNS → Oligodendrocyte → myelin

  • Astrocyte → support, BBB, ionic regulation

  • Microglia → phagocytic immune cells

  • Ependymal cells → line ventricles and central canal

High-yield Neuroglia recall:
Schwann = PNS myelin
Oligodendrocyte = CNS myelin

Exam pearl:
“Schwann in PNS = Oligodendrocyte in CNS.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ১৮) Eccrine sweat glands are most numerous on the.......?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
Eccrine sweat glands are distributed widely over the body but are particularly numerous on the palms and soles. Among the given options, the soles are the best answer.

They are important for thermoregulation and are not associated with hair follicles.

High-yield Skin histology recall:
Eccrine glands → especially numerous on palms and soles.

Exam pearl:
“Eccrine sweat glands are most numerous on palms and soles.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ১৯) Which is the principal signal reception and processing sites on neurons?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
Dendrites are the principal sites for receiving and processing incoming signals from other neurons. They contain numerous receptors and synaptic contacts and conduct signals toward the cell body.

  • Dendrites → receive incoming signals

  • Cell body → metabolic and integrative functions

  • Axon → conducts impulses away from the cell body

  • Axon hillock → initiates action potential

High-yield Neurophysiology recall:
Dendrites = reception
Axon = transmission

Exam pearl:
“Dendrites receive; axons transmit.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ২০) Sebaceous glands are present in which layer of skin?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
Sebaceous glands are located mainly in the reticular layer of the dermis, usually associated with hair follicles. They secrete sebum, which lubricates and protects the skin and hair.

  • Reticular dermis → sebaceous glands

  • Epidermis → no sebaceous glands

  • Papillary dermis → mainly loose connective tissue and dermal papillae

  • Subcutaneous layer → mainly adipose tissue

High-yield Skin histology recall:
Sebaceous gland → dermis → usually associated with hair follicle → holocrine secretion.

Exam pearl:
“Sebaceous gland = reticular dermis + holocrine secretion.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ২১) Lamellated or pacinian corpuscles on skin are designed for detection of.......?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
Pacinian (lamellated) corpuscles are rapidly adapting mechanoreceptors that are especially sensitive to high-frequency vibration and deep pressure.

  • Pacinian corpuscle → vibration + deep pressure

  • Meissner corpuscle → light touch

  • Free nerve endings → pain and temperature

  • Ruffini endings → skin stretch/warmth

Exam pearl:
“Pacinian = Vibration.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ২২) Which glial cells are located at PNS?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
Satellite cells are glial cells of the peripheral nervous system (PNS). They surround the cell bodies of neurons in peripheral ganglia and provide structural, metabolic, and protective support.

  • Satellite cells → PNS

  • Schwann cells → PNS myelination

  • Oligodendrocytes → CNS myelination

  • Microglia → CNS phagocytic cells

  • Ependymal cells → CNS ventricles and central canal

High-yield Neuroglia recall:
PNS glia → Schwann + Satellite cells
CNS glia → Oligodendrocyte + Astrocyte + Microglia + Ependymal cells

Exam pearl:
“Satellite = PNS ganglia.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ২৩) Dermis has how many major layers?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
The dermis has two major layers:

  1. Papillary layer — superficial, made of loose connective tissue.

  2. Reticular layer — deeper, made of dense irregular connective tissue.

High-yield Skin anatomy recall:
Dermis = Papillary + Reticular

Exam pearl:
“Dermis has 2 layers: papillary and reticular.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ২৪) Which neuroglial cell is originated from bone marrow?
২৫) Which structure typifies reticular dermis but not papillary dermis?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
The reticular dermis is composed mainly of dense irregular connective tissue, containing abundant collagen and elastic fibers. This provides strength and tensile resistance to the skin.

  • Reticular dermis → dense irregular connective tissue

  • Papillary dermis → loose areolar connective tissue

  • Meissner corpuscles → mainly papillary dermis

  • Capillary loops → prominent in papillary dermis

  • Sweat glands/ducts → mainly deeper dermis

High-yield Skin histology recall:
Papillary dermis = loose CT
Reticular dermis = dense irregular CT

Exam pearl:
“Reticular = dense irregular connective tissue.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ২৬) Which neuroglial cell assists in production and circulation of cerebrospinal fluid?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
Ependymal cells line the ventricles of the brain and central canal of the spinal cord. Specialized ependymal cells in the choroid plexus help in the production of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), while their cilia help facilitate CSF circulation.

  • Ependymal cells → CSF production & circulation

  • Oligodendrocytes → CNS myelination

  • Satellite cells → support neurons in PNS ganglia

  • Microglia → CNS immune/phagocytic function

Exam pearl:
“Ependymal cells = CSF.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ২৭) Myoepithelial cells aid in the secretory process of which of the following?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
Myoepithelial cells are contractile cells located between the secretory epithelial cells and basement membrane of certain glands. Their contraction helps expel glandular secretions.

They are classically associated with eccrine sweat glands and also occur around secretory portions of some other exocrine glands.

  • Eccrine sweat glands → myoepithelial cells aid secretion

  • Sebaceous glands → holocrine secretion

  • Keratinocytes → not a gland

  • Apocrine glands → may also contain myoepithelial cells, but the classic MCQ answer is eccrine sweat gland

Exam pearl:
“Myoepithelial cells contract → squeeze out glandular secretion.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ২৮) What is the dermatome of anus?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
The perianal skin/anus is classically supplied by the S4–S5 dermatomes, with S5 being the specific answer in this MCQ.

High-yield Dermatome recall:

  • T10 → Umbilicus

  • L1 → Inguinal region

  • S2 → Posterior thigh

  • S4–S5 → Perianal region

Exam pearl:
“Anus = S5 (with S4 contribution).”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ২৯) Which neuroglial cell provides structural support and organization to the central nervous system?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
Astrocytes are the major supporting glial cells of the CNS. They provide structural support, help maintain the extracellular environment, contribute to the blood–brain barrier, and support neuronal metabolism.

  • Astrocytes → structural & metabolic support of CNS

  • Oligodendrocytes → myelination of CNS axons

  • Ependymal cells → line ventricles and help with CSF

  • Satellite cells → support neurons in PNS ganglia

High-yield Neuroglia recall:
Astrocyte → support
Oligodendrocyte → myelin
Microglia → macrophage
Ependymal → CSF

Exam pearl:
“Astrocytes = structural support cells of the CNS.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ৩০) Which acts as Extrinsic eye muscle attachment site?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
The extraocular (extrinsic) muscles attach primarily to the sclera, the tough fibrous outer coat of the eyeball. Their contraction moves the eyeball in different directions.

  • Sclera → attachment of extraocular muscles

  • Cornea → transparent anterior part of fibrous coat

  • Choroid → vascular middle layer

  • Iris → controls pupil diameter

High-yield Eye anatomy recall:
Extraocular muscles → Sclera

Exam pearl:
“Sclera = attachment site for extrinsic eye muscles.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ৩১) Which is not a histological layer of cerebellar cortex?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
The cerebellar cortex has three histological layers:

  1. Molecular layer — outermost

  2. Purkinje cell layer — middle

  3. Granular layer — innermost

Pyramidal cells are characteristic neurons of the cerebral cortex, not a layer of the cerebellar cortex.

High-yield Neuroanatomy recall:
Cerebellar cortex → Molecular → Purkinje → Granular

Exam pearl:
“Cerebellum has 3 layers; pyramidal cells belong to the cerebral cortex.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ৩২) Which Supplies nourishment to retina?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
The choroid is a highly vascular layer located between the sclera and retina. Its rich blood supply provides oxygen and nutrients to the outer retina, particularly the photoreceptor cells.

  • Choroid → nourishes outer retina

  • Sclera → protection and structural support

  • Cornea → transparent, avascular structure

  • Iris → controls pupil size

High-yield Eye anatomy recall:
Choroid = vascular layer → nourishes outer retina.

Exam pearl:
“Choroid supplies nourishment to the retina.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ৩৩) The main structural component of the BBB is the.....?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.option2: limiting layer of perivascular astrocytic feet
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
The main structural component of the blood–brain barrier (BBB) is the capillary endothelial cells, which are joined by tight junctions and have very low permeability.

Other components include:

  • Basement membrane

  • Perivascular astrocytic end-feet — supportive role

  • Pericytes

High-yield Neuroanatomy recall:
BBB → continuous capillary endothelium + tight junctions + basement membrane + astrocytic support.

Exam pearl:
“Main structural component of BBB = capillary endothelium with tight junctions.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ৩৪) Which layer of eyeball Provides vitamin A for photoreceptor cells?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
The retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) plays a crucial role in the visual cycle, including the storage and regeneration of vitamin A derivatives (retinoids) needed by photoreceptor cells for synthesis and regeneration of visual pigments.

  • Pigmented layer of retina → vitamin A/retinoid metabolism + photoreceptor support

  • Choroid → vascular supply to the outer retina

  • Neural retina → contains photoreceptors and other neurons

  • Iris → regulates the amount of light entering the eye

Exam pearl:
“RPE = photoreceptor support + visual cycle + vitamin A/retinoid metabolism.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ৩৫) Immediately around the external lamina of the Schwann cells is a thin layer called the.......?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
The endoneurium is a delicate connective tissue layer that surrounds individual nerve fibers (axons with their Schwann cells). It lies immediately outside the external lamina (basal lamina) of Schwann cells.

  • Endoneurium → surrounds individual nerve fiber

  • Perineurium → surrounds a bundle/fascicle of nerve fibers

  • Epineurium → surrounds the entire peripheral nerve

  • Fascicle → bundle of nerve fibers, not a connective tissue layer

High-yield Peripheral nerve recall:
Nerve fiber → Endoneurium → Fascicle → Perineurium → Whole nerve → Epineurium

Exam pearl:

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ৩৬) Which Controls pupil diameter and thus the amount of light entering the eye?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
The iris controls the diameter of the pupil, thereby regulating the amount of light entering the eye.

  • Bright light → circular sphincter pupillae contracts → pupil constricts (miosis)

  • Dim light → radial dilator pupillae contracts → pupil dilates (mydriasis)

High-yield Eye physiology recall:
Iris → pupil diameter → controls light entry.

Exam pearl:
“Iris = camera aperture of the eye.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ৩৭) What term applies to collections of neuronal cell bodies (somata) in the central nervous system?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
In the central nervous system (CNS), collections of neuronal cell bodies (somata) are called nuclei.

  • CNS → Nuclei

  • PNS → Ganglia

  • Neuroglia → supporting cells of the nervous system

  • Nodes → not the term for collections of neuronal cell bodies

High-yield Neuroanatomy recall:
“Nuclei in CNS; ganglia in PNS.”

Exam pearl:
CNS = Nuclei | PNS = Ganglia

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ৩৮) A subcapsular lens epithelium consists of a single layer of........... cells present only on the anterior surface of the lens?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
The lens epithelium consists of a single layer of cuboidal epithelial cells located only on the anterior surface of the lens, beneath the lens capsule.

  • Lens epithelium → simple cuboidal

  • Present only anteriorly

  • Posterior surface → no epithelial layer

  • These cells help maintain lens metabolism and can differentiate into lens fibers near the equator.

Exam pearl:
“Lens epithelium = single layer of cuboidal cells on the anterior surface.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ৩৯) Which structure contains trabeculae around which cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) flows?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
The arachnoid mater forms arachnoid trabeculae, delicate connective tissue strands that extend across the subarachnoid space. CSF flows through this space around the trabeculae.

  • Arachnoid mater → trabeculae + subarachnoid space containing CSF

  • Pia mater → closely adheres to the brain and spinal cord surface

  • Dura mater → tough outer meningeal layer

  • Ependyma → lines brain ventricles and central canal

Exam pearl:
“Arachnoid trabeculae span the CSF-filled subarachnoid space.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ৪০) The only cells in the vitreous body are a small mesenchymal population near the membrane called.......?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
Hyalocytes are the principal cells found in the vitreous body. They are a small population of mesenchymal-derived cells, located mainly near the vitreous cortex and hyaloid membrane. They help maintain the vitreous matrix and participate in its turnover.

  • Hyalocytes → vitreous body

  • Melanocytes → pigmented tissues

  • Collagenase → enzyme, not a cell

  • Coagulocyte → not a normal vitreous cell

Exam pearl:
“Vitreous body cells = Hyalocytes.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ৪১) Which is not a content of Uveal tract ?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
The uveal tract (uvea) is the middle, vascular layer of the eyeball and consists of:

  1. Choroid

  2. Ciliary body

  3. Iris

The cornea is part of the fibrous outer coat, not the uveal tract.

High-yield Eye anatomy recall:
Uvea = Choroid + Ciliary body + Iris

Exam pearl:
“Cornea is not part of uvea.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ৪২) Which is the largest single organ of the body?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
The skin is the largest single organ of the human body by both surface area and weight. It covers the entire external surface and acts as a protective barrier.

  • Skin → largest organ

  • Liver → largest internal organ

  • Neuron → functional cell, not an organ

  • Hair → skin appendage

Exam pearl:
“Skin = largest organ; Liver = largest internal organ.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ৪৩) What is the lining epithelium of conjunctiva?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
The conjunctiva is lined by stratified columnar epithelium, typically with goblet cells that contribute to the tear film.

  • Conjunctiva → stratified columnar epithelium

  • Goblet cells → mucus secretion

  • Cornea → stratified squamous non-keratinized epithelium

Exam pearl:
“Conjunctiva = stratified columnar epithelium with goblet cells.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ৪৪) Which one is tactile epithelial cells of skin?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
Merkel cells are specialized tactile epithelial cells located mainly in the stratum basale of the epidermis. They are associated with sensory nerve endings and detect fine touch/pressure.

  • Merkel cells → tactile sensation

  • Keratinocytes → keratin production and barrier

  • Melanocytes → melanin production

  • Langerhans cells → antigen presentation

Exam pearl:
“Merkel = tactile cell of skin.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ৪৫) What is the Sensory Receptor of cochlea?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
The spiral organ (Organ of Corti) is the sensory receptor organ of the cochlea. It contains inner and outer hair cells, which convert mechanical vibrations caused by sound into electrical nerve signals.

  • Spiral organ/Organ of Corti → hearing

  • Maculae → linear acceleration & static equilibrium

  • Cristae ampullares → angular acceleration

  • Semicircular ducts → rotational movement/balance

Exam pearl:
“Cochlea → Organ of Corti → hearing.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ৪৬) Which one is the deepest layer of skin epidermis?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
Stratum basale is the deepest layer of the epidermis, lying directly on the basement membrane and adjacent to the dermis.

It contains:

  • Basal keratinocytes → continuous cell renewal

  • Melanocytes → melanin production

  • Merkel cells → tactile sensation

Epidermal layers (deep → superficial):
Basale → Spinosum → Granulosum → Lucidum → Corneum*

*Stratum lucidum is present only in thick skin.

Exam pearl:
“Deepest epidermal layer = stratum basale.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ৪৭) Which layer of epidermis protects against friction and water loss?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
The stratum corneum is the outermost layer of the epidermis and provides the main protective barrier against friction, mechanical injury, pathogens, and water loss.

  • Stratum corneum → keratinized cells + lipid barrier → protection & prevents water loss

  • Stratum granulosum → contributes to keratinization and waterproofing

  • Stratum spinosum → provides mechanical strength

  • Stratum basale → cell renewal and melanocytes

Exam pearl:
“Stratum corneum = main barrier against friction and water loss.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ৪৮) The part of the nerve fibre between two nodes of Ranvier is called the.....?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
The internode is the segment of a myelinated nerve fiber between two successive Nodes of Ranvier. It is covered by a continuous myelin sheath formed by Schwann cells in the PNS or oligodendrocytes in the CNS.

  • Node of Ranvier → gap between myelin segments

  • Internode → segment between two nodes

  • Neurite → general term for axon or dendrite

  • Axolemma → cell membrane of the axon

Exam pearl:
“Between two Nodes of Ranvier = Internode.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ৪৯) Which is not true about axon?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
Nissl granules (Nissl bodies) are present in the cell body and dendrites, but they are absent from the axon and axon hillock.

  • Axon → usually single per neuron

  • Axon → generally a long process

  • Axon → may be myelinated or unmyelinated

  • Nissl granules → absent in axon

High-yield Neurohistology recall:
Nissl bodies → soma + dendrites
No Nissl bodies → axon + axon hillock

Exam pearl:
“Nissl granules are absent from the axon.”

Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.question: ৫০) Mitosis occurs in which layer of epidermis?
Nervous system & special sense, Skin, De.exp:
Mitosis mainly occurs in the stratum basale (stratum germinativum), where basal keratinocytes continuously divide to produce new epidermal cells.

Give feedback

  • Stratum basale → active mitosis and cell renewal

  • Stratum spinosum → mainly maturation

  • Stratum granulosum → keratinization

  • Stratum corneum → dead, keratinized cells

Exam pearl:
“Mitosis = Stratum basale.”
